title: Driver Quality Standards Bulletin: The Wayfare Rating Standard
content:
The rating standard applies to every agreement under the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product. Its level figures (minimum rating to keep, rating window, rated trips needed, fallback agreement, days to the deciding review, warnings before deactivation) are in the rating standard schedule.

## Standard

**(a) When it acts.** The rating standard acts only on an active agreement with at least the level's rated trips needed for action in the rating window; the rating is the average of the most recent rating-window rated trips, compared at two decimal places.

**(b) Fallback.** When the rating is below the level's minimum rating to keep and the level has a fallback agreement whose own minimum rating to keep the rating still meets, the agreement is moved to that level instead of being warned.

**(c) Warning and review.** Otherwise a rating below the minimum rating to keep brings a rating warning. At the rating review held the level's reassessment days after the warning, a rating still below the standard of the level then held leads to deactivation for rating below minimum once the level's number of rating warnings before deactivation are on record within the warning validity days; a rating at or above it closes the matter.

**(d) Reversal.** A rating deactivation is never appealed; it is reversed only through the quality improvement course.

## Evidence

The agreement's status, its rated trips in the window and the rating reviews and warnings on the standing record are system records tied to that agreement.

## Outcome table

| Rating against the level's minimum | Fallback level exists and its minimum is met | Result |
|---|---|---|
| at or above | (not read) | no action |
| below | yes | moved to the fallback level, no warning |
| below | no | rating warning |

| At the deciding rating review | Result |
|---|---|
| still below the standard of the level then held, required warnings on record within the validity days | deactivation for rating below minimum |
| at or above that standard | the matter is closed |

## Hypothetical cases

- A Wayfare Comfort driver with 300 rated trips in the window and a rating of 4.75: below the Comfort minimum of 4.80, and the Wayfare Standard fallback minimum of 4.60 is met, so the agreement moves to Wayfare Standard without a warning.
- A Wayfare Standard driver with a rating of 4.55: Standard has no fallback, so a rating warning is given.
- A driver with 80 rated trips in the window: below the 100 needed, so the standard does not act.
